messages:
noah: Heads-up — onboarding quickpack for customer Caspian (LoRA adapter merge) is showing a regression in monetary formatting after int4 quant. Repro steps + minimal outputs below. Need a quick triage before we promote this to dedicated pools.

katie: Ugh, thanks. Is this from the standard quick-eval set or a customer-provided prompt set?

noah: It’s the customer promptpack + our currency checks. Quick-eval summary from local run: 

```
quick-eval: caspian-adapter v0.3.1 + base-cascade-int4
tests run: 120
failed: 3
failure types: currency_format, thousands_separator, embed-shift
example input: "Total due: $1,234.56"
expected: "$1,234.56"
actual: "1234.56 USD"
```

sasha: Which quant pipeline did you use? GPTQ or AWQ? Also which tokenizer version for this run?

noah: GPTQ-4bit recipe from infra (gptq-2025-04), tokenizer v14. We reuse the same tokenizers as hosted. The odd part is comma separators are dropped for some locale-sensitive templates.

ravi: Can you paste the exact command you ran? I’ll try to reproduce on a warm pool.

noah: Sure — repro command: 
```
./ci/run_quickpack.sh \
  --client caspian \
  --adapter lora/caspian-v0.3.1 \
  --base-model cascade-base-3b \
  --quant gptq-4bit \
  --prompts tests/caspian_currency.jsonl \
  --out tmp/caspian_qpack.out
```

eval-bot: quick-eval results uploaded: s3://redwood-test-results/caspian/3851234567/summary.json — 3 failures — see failing cases list. :warning:

katie: Quick thoughts — currency formatting often breaks when token alignment shifts around punctuation after quantization; comma tokenization sometimes merges into numeric tokens. Two short mitigations: 1) route currency-heavy queries to fp16 variant for now; 2) add a post-processing patch in the eval harness that prefers locale-aware formatting when a money entity is detected (cheap guard).

noah: Agreed. I'd prefer a short-term routing fallback (fp16) + small token remap test next. We should also run a diff across tokenizer merges for the adapter.

sasha: I can spin a canary in dedicated with route rule: caspian_currency -> base-cascade-fp16 for 100% of requests matching regex. When do you want the canary? I can schedule a low-traffic window and monitor.

ravi: Also open a quick PR to the quant recipe: try forcing byte-pair re-split for comma-adjacent numbers (hacky but quick). If it reduces failures we can bake a clean tokenizer mapping later.

katie: Please also add the failing prompt examples to the regression suite and tag them with customer-caspian so we catch regressions in the future.

noah: Will add examples to tests/caspian_currency.jsonl now. I’ll also run the tokenizer diff and paste the smallest reproducer here.

noah: Minimal reproducer output: 
```
input: "Amount: $12,345.67"
fp16-output: "$12,345.67"
int4-output: "12345.67 USD"
tokenized(fp16): ["Amount", ":", " ", "$", "12", ",", "345", ".", "67"]
tokenized(int4): ["Amount", ":", " ", "$", "12345", ".", "67"]
```

sasha: That tokenized diff is exactly the culprit — comma got swallowed into numeric token under the quant tokenizer rewrite. I’ll patch the quant preprocessor to prefer a split on "," when adjacent to digits for this adapter.

deploy-bot: schedule: canary-deploy/caspian-tokenfix @ 2025-05-10T21:30:00Z — created by sasha — target pool: dedicated-canary-3 

noah: Thanks. After the patch we should re-run quickpack and confirm failures drop to 0/120. If green, we can roll forward a canary for 10% traffic then 50%.

katie: For rollout plan: canary 10% (2h), monitor quick-eval + telemetry for currency ops; if >99.5% correct then 50% (2h); then full. Also create a rollback rule to the previous float variant.

sasha: Will action. I’ll post the canary link when live.

deploy-bot: deployment started: canary-deploy/caspian-tokenfix on dedicated-canary-3 — job 98765 — logs: https://deploys.redwood.dev/jobs/98765

noah: Running fresh quick-eval now, will paste results in ~10m.

eval-bot: quick-eval run complete for job 98765 — passed 120/120 (regressions cleared) — details: s3://redwood-test-results/caspian/3851234567/postpatch-summary.json :tada:

noah: Nice — moving to canary rollout per plan. Thanks all for the fast turnaround. :raised_hands:
